subject: Post-call: clarify sessionized QPS, token deltas & streaming mix
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor Hayes <connor@cartgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: clarify sessionized QPS, token deltas & streaming mix

Hi Connor —

Thanks again for the 30-minute sync this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so our infra/ops team can size a pilot cluster and produce a draft SLA. Can you confirm the points below (we captured approximate numbers on the call but want them in writing):

1) Steady-state vs peaks
  - Steady (baseline) QPS: you mentioned ~12 QPS for the user-facing inference endpoint — is that per-region or global?
  - Typical peak windows: you said there are short crest events driven by promotional activity — how long are the crests (sustained seconds/minutes)?

2) Tokens per request
  - Median tokens per inference: ~350 tokens (prompt + completion) — please confirm median and 95th.
  - Are there multi-turn sessions where cumulative tokens are significantly higher? If so, how many requests per session on average?

3) Streaming usage and concurrency
  - What fraction of requests will use streaming responses vs non-streamed completions?
  - For streaming sessions: approximate per-session token/sec emission (tokens/sec) and average session duration.

4) Latency targets (SLO)
  - Non-streaming: target p95 inference latency goal (end-to-end).
  - Streaming: initial chunk time-to-first-token goal and per-chunk latency target.

5) Operational artifacts
  - If you can share a 24-hour event sample (anonymized request-level rows: timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, is_streaming, region), that will accelerate sizing.

Next steps (proposed):
- You share sample event file and confirm numbers above (tokens and peak window lengths).
- Ops run quick capacity model and return a recommended pilot config + estimated monthly committed cost.
- We do a 2-week pilot (dedicated pool) with simple SLOs and a rollback plan.

I attached the call recording and a short template to paste a small sample of events (if easier). Thanks — aiming to have a pilot recommendation by Wednesday EOD once we get the sample.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: call-recording-20270512.mp3, session-sample-events-20270512.jsonl
From: Connor Hayes <connor@cartgrid.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@cartgrid.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: clarify sessionized QPS, token deltas & streaming mix

Laura — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming numbers below (we pulled a quick sample from last week's traffic):

1) Steady vs peaks
  - Baseline/global QPS: 12 QPS (this is global; our EU traffic is ~25% of that).
  - Peak crests: we see short bursts driven by scheduled sends and promotions — typical crest lasts 45-120s. Peak crest QPS can spike up to ~240 QPS (we throttle at the edge but bursts get through).

2) Tokens per request
  - Median total tokens (prompt+completion): 340 tokens. 95th percentile: ~1,200 tokens (rare long completions).
  - Multi-turn sessions: ~3.2 requests/session on average; ~9% of sessions exceed 8 requests.

3) Streaming usage and concurrency
  - Streaming fraction: ~30% of requests are streamed (mostly interactive features).
  - For streamed sessions: per-session emission ~60-90 tokens/sec depending on model; average streamed session duration ~22s.
  - Concurrent streaming sessions during peaks: we see up to ~18 concurrent streams during crest windows (global).

4) Latency targets
  - Non-streaming: target p95 <= 400ms (end-to-end from request to final token).
  - Streaming: TTF (time-to-first-token) goal <= 600ms, steady-state per-chunk latency <= 200ms.

5) Artifacts
  - Attached: small anonymized sample (we removed user IDs). Let me know if the format works.

Happy to hop on a quick call if you have follow-ups.

—Connor
Connor Hayes
Head of Product | CartGrid
connor@cartgrid.com

Attachments: session-sample-events-20270512.jsonl
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor Hayes <connor@cartgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: clarify sessionized QPS, token deltas & streaming mix

Connor — perfect, this is exactly what we needed. A few follow-ups and clarifications from ops side (we want to avoid over-provisioning for the crest shape):

- Crest handling: you said peaks can reach 240 QPS for ~45–120s. Can you share timestamps of a couple of representative crests (we only need 3–5 windows) so we can model realistic crest overlap across regions?

- Concurrent streams: 18 concurrent streams at peak (global) — is that sustained for the entire crest window or a short pulse inside the crest? Ops asks because streaming holds resources longer per session vs non-streaming.

- Backpressure and retries: do clients retry aggressively on 5xx/429s? If yes, what's the retry backoff pattern (helps with tail sizing).

Operational ask: attached is a tiny event-template (JSONL column order: ts,is_streaming,tokens_in,tokens_out,region,session_id). If you can paste a 2-hour slice (even sampled) we can run the pilot sizing immediately.

We'll produce: a recommended pilot pool (GPU counts, concurrency per GPU, expected p95 latency under baseline and crest with simulated bursts), and a short runbook for crest handling (auto-burst policy + graceful fallback to smaller model). Target to send that by tomorrow EOD.

Thanks again — copying Marissa and Jonas for sizing sign-off.

Best,
Laura

Cc: Connor Hayes <connor@cartgrid.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: clarify sessionized QPS, token deltas & streaming mix

Looping in a couple of quick ops notes after looking at the sample Connor provided:

- Pilot sizing (initial recommendation)
  - Start with a 4-GPU dedicated pool (A100-equivalent), configured with: 16 streaming concurrency slots per GPU, 64 non-stream concurrency per GPU.
  - Simulate crest by replaying the 45–120s windows with a 5x traffic multiplication to validate headroom; target keeps p95 <= 450ms during crest (we'll tune to meet the 400ms goal).

- Caching and prefix reuse
  - For multi-turn sessions (average 3.2 requests/session) we'll enable prefix KV caching where applicable to shave tokens_out and reduce compute. Expect ~8–12% lower GPU time on repeated prompts.

- Fallback policy suggestion
  - If p95 degrades >20% during crest for >60s, automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model variant for non-stream traffic and prioritized serving for streaming sessions.

Marissa will produce the pilot config and rough cost estimate and share in the Drive link. Connor — if you can provide the 2-hour sample slice and 3 crest timestamps, we'll finalize the pilot doc today.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Performance Ops | Redwood Inference
